edict.aliveworkplace.festival_season.des: A festival every 4 days instead of 8; each costs the treasury 3 emeralds and 1 more for every 4 villagers, and with no money there's no festival and the village is disappointed.
edict.aliveworkplace.tithe.desc: A tenth of the emeralds players pay the villagers in trades goes into the treasury; their emerald prices are 10% higher.
edict.aliveworkplace.curfew.desc: From dusk to dawn everyone but the guards and mercenaries stays in bed, safe from monsters, and raids are half as likely; but nobody trades at night, festivals end at dusk without fireworks, market traders leave at dusk and nobody sets out after midday.
edict.aliveworkplace.conscription.desc: In a raid every grown villager who isn't ill takes up a stone sword and fights beside the guards; but all work stops during the raid and until noon the next day, and the conscripts can fall like anyone else.

reform.aliveworkplace.shift_bell.line: A bell in the yard calls the shifts, so nobody works past their hour.
reform.aliveworkplace.common_granary.lin: A granary keeps the bread line, so the free bread no longer eats into the store.
reform.aliveworkplace.midwives.line: Midwives see every mother and child through, so big families need no more food and fall ill no more often.
reform.aliveworkplace.watchful_gate.line: A gate watch that knows every face: travelers keep coming, and bandits are no likelier to make camp than usual.
reform.aliveworkplace.festival_fund.line: The villagers put by for their own festivals: one every 4 days, and the treasury pays nothing.
reform.aliveworkplace.fair_ledger.line: The tithe comes out of the takings, not the price: the treasury keeps its tenth and prices are back to normal.
reform.aliveworkplace.lamplighters.line: Lamplit streets, so the curfew can end at the door: raids stay half as likely and the nights safe, but trading, festivals, markets and night work go on.
reform.aliveworkplace.militia_drill.line: Drilled at the dummies, the militia fights without stopping the village: everyone still fights, but work stops only near a raider and the morning after is a normal day.

tooltip.aliveworkplace.guide_book: Right-click to read how villagers' jobs work
guide.aliveworkplace.intro: Villagers here do real work. Each page shows one thing in the game and how to do it. Turn the pages with the arrows, the arrow keys or the mouse wheel, or pick a chapter.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.welcome.title: Villagers with real jobs
guide.aliveworkplace.page.welcome.text: Builders put up houses from blueprints, miners dig quarries, farmers farm and guards fight. Workers keep their tools and their work in the chests near their workstation, and most work by day and sleep at night.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.camp.title: No village? Bring settlers
guide.aliveworkplace.page.camp.text: Craft a Settler's Wagon and right-click open ground. Two settlers make camp by a Blueprint Table, with a chest of supplies and a Village Hall to place. The first one is already a builder; give the other a job.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.jobs.title: Give a villager a job
guide.aliveworkplace.page.jobs.text: Most jobs share a vanilla workstation. Stand a villager by it, hold the job's item and sneak-right-click them: sweet berries at a composter make an Orchard Keeper. Hold Shift over a workstation in your inventory to see its jobs.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.status.title: What is a worker doing?
guide.aliveworkplace.page.status.text: A worker's job and what they're busy with float over their head. Sneak-right-click a builder, miner or farmer with an empty hand for the full status and how to stop them.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.table.title: Hire a builder
guide.aliveworkplace.page.table.text: Place a Blueprint Table near a villager without a job: they become a Builder. Villages often have a builder's workshop already. Buy blueprints from the builder; more unlock as they level up.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.place.title: Place a blueprint
guide.aliveworkplace.page.place.text: Hold the blueprint and right-click the ground where the front should go. The whole building shows as see-through blocks, and its gold edge is the front. Sneak-right-click the ground to turn it.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.stock.title: Stock the chests
guide.aliveworkplace.page.stock.text: Put the materials in chests or barrels within 8 blocks of the Blueprint Table. Hold Shift over the placed blueprint: it counts what the chests are still short of.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.build.title: Hand it over
guide.aliveworkplace.page.build.text: Right-click the builder with the blueprint. They clear the site, fetch the blocks and build it by day. A busy builder takes up to 5 more. To have a building taken down, place its blueprint over it and sneak as you hand it over.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.styles.title: Styles and upgrades
guide.aliveworkplace.page.styles.text: Sneak-right-click the air with a blueprint to build it in Stonework, Sandstone, Dark Oak or Cherry, or mirrored. Most buildings have an upgrade: place it over the finished one and only what's new gets built.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.library.title: The Blueprint Table
guide.aliveworkplace.page.library.text: Right-click the table to see every blueprint and what it needs. Get Blueprint copies one onto a Blank Blueprint. Upload a File adds your own .litematic or .schem builds for everyone.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.shapes.title: Your own designs
guide.aliveworkplace.page.shapes.text: A Scan Tool saves something you built as a blueprint: right-click two corners, then sneak-right-click the air. The Shape Planner draws walls, towers, domes and arches as blueprints.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.hall.title: The Village Hall
guide.aliveworkplace.page.hall.text: Craft a Village Hall and put it in the middle of your village. Right-click it to see beds, food, guards, what the workers are waiting for and everyone within 64 blocks. Each morning it posts a quest.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.people.title: Your villagers
guide.aliveworkplace.page.people.text: With a hall, villagers get names, traits and moods. They eat from the village store and like a bed of their own. Click one on the hall's list to make them glow so you can find them.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.requests.title: What the village needs
guide.aliveworkplace.page.requests.text: The hall lists everything the workers are waiting for. Hand it over at a Storehouse, or right-click the Storehouse and click a request to send what you carry straight to that worker.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.storehouse.tex: Craft a Storehouse and put chests near it: a villager without a job becomes its Porter. The porter carries what the other workers make to its chests and leaves them the tools they need.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.villages.title: Villages grow
guide.aliveworkplace.page.villages.text: Villages grow workshops, guard houses, clinics, post offices, kitchens and inns by themselves. With a hall a village ranks up from Hamlet to City and keeps a chronicle of what happened there.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.city_plan.text: Craft a City Plan (a map, a Blank Blueprint and a Heart of the Sea) and bind it to the hall. Right-click the air to paint zones, streets and a wall line. Sneak-right-click a Journeyman Builder by the hall with it: as Steward he builds the village into the plan.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.miner.title: Miner
guide.aliveworkplace.page.miner.text: A pickaxe at a blast furnace makes a Miner. Mark a quarry's two corners with a Quarry Marker and give it to them. Keep pickaxes and torches in a chest near the furnace; they bring the stone and ore back.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.lumberjack.tex: An axe at a fletching table near some trees makes a Lumberjack. They fell the trees within 16 blocks and plant a sapling where each stood. Keep axes and a few saplings in a chest nearby.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.farmer.title: Farmer
guide.aliveworkplace.page.farmer.text: Mark a field's two corners with a Field Marker and give it to a farmer (the villager at a composter). Put seeds in a chest near the composter: they harvest, replant and sow the field.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.orchard.title: Orchard Keeper
guide.aliveworkplace.page.orchard.text: Sweet berries, glow berries or an apple at a composter in your orchard make an Orchard Keeper. They pick everything ripe within 16 blocks: berries and cocoa pods.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.fisher.title: Fisherman
guide.aliveworkplace.page.fisher.text: Hand a fisherman (the villager at a barrel) a fishing rod. They fish near their barrel and bring the catch back. Put a boat in their barrel and they row out onto open water.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.beekeeper.text: A glass bottle or shears by a beehive makes a Beekeeper. A flower at a composter makes a Florist, bone meal a Composter, gravel at a cauldron a Sifter. Hold Shift over a workstation for its jobs.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.carpenter.text: Planks at a crafting table make a Carpenter. When a builder nearby is short of something that can be crafted, like fences or doors, the carpenter makes it from the chests and takes it over.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.chef.title: Chef
guide.aliveworkplace.page.chef.text: Raw food at a smoker makes a Chef. Put the makings in a chest nearby and the chef cooks bread, pies, stews and roasts for the village store.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.mail.title: Mail
guide.aliveworkplace.page.mail.text: Craft a Mailbox and place it: mail for you arrives there. Put items in the top row, write a player's name and press Send. Paper by a mailbox makes a Postman, who carries the parcels.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.shop.title: Your shop
guide.aliveworkplace.page.shop.text: Place a Shop Counter near a villager without a job: they become your Shopkeeper. Open the counter to set what each sale gives and its price, and keep the goods in chests nearby.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.ferry.title: Ferries
guide.aliveworkplace.page.ferry.text: Place Travel Posts in your villages and right-click them to learn them. A villager without a job at a post becomes its Ferryman and sells tickets to your other posts, and rows you there.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.guard.title: Guard
guide.aliveworkplace.page.guard.text: A sword at a grindstone makes a Guard. Put weapons and armor in a chest nearby: the guard takes the best. Guards fight monsters within 24 blocks at any hour, and ride a saddled horse or camel.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.training.title: Patrols and training
guide.aliveworkplace.page.training.text: Mark up to eight spots with a Patrol Map and sneak-right-click a guard with it. A Training Dummy near the grindstone keeps guards sparring. Raise a Rally Banner and enlisted guards follow you.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.nurse.title: Nurse
guide.aliveworkplace.page.nurse.text: A honey bottle at a brewing stand makes a Nurse. Right-click the nurse with an empty hand to get your health back. Nurses also cure the village's ill with honey bottles from their chest.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.trainer.title: Trainer
guide.aliveworkplace.page.trainer.text: Place a Training Post near a villager without a job: they become a Trainer. Right-click them with an empty hand to battle. They rank up as people battle them, from Novice to Master.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.tutor.title: Move Tutor
guide.aliveworkplace.page.tutor.text: A book at a Training Post makes a Move Tutor. Right-click them, pick one of your Pokémon and a move it can't learn by leveling. Click the lesson again to pay and teach it.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.ball_smith.tex: An apricorn at a smithing table makes a Ball Smith. Keep apricorns and copper, iron, gold or diamonds in chests nearby and they make Poké Balls with Cobblemon's recipes.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.trader.title: Pokémon Trader
guide.aliveworkplace.page.trader.text: A Poké Ball at a Shop Counter makes a Pokémon Trader. Right-click them for today's offers, pick one and one of your Pokémon that fits, and click it twice to swap.
guide.aliveworkplace.page.fossil.title: Fossil Scientist
guide.aliveworkplace.page.fossil.text: A fossil at Cobblemon's Fossil Analyzer makes a Fossil Scientist. Hand them a fossil and pay: they revive it while they work, and the Pokémon joins your party.

screen.aliveworkplace.calendar.about: Four seasons of %s days, the same for every village, each with a festival on its middle day

aliveworkplace.config.title: Alive Workplace Settings
aliveworkplace.config.note: For this computer's worlds; a server keeps its own config file.
aliveworkplace.config.supplyRadius.toolt: Chests and barrels within this many blocks of a workstation are that villager's supply chests.
aliveworkplace.config.maxSiteDistance.to: How far from their Blueprint Table, in blocks, a builder takes a build outside the village. Anywhere in the village the table stands in is always in reach.
aliveworkplace.config.quarryReach.toolti: How far from their Miner's Bench, in blocks, a miner takes a quarry outside the village. Anywhere in the village the bench stands in is always in reach.
aliveworkplace.config.fieldReach.tooltip: How far from their composter, in blocks, a farmer takes a marked field outside the village. Anywhere in the village the composter stands in is always in reach.
aliveworkplace.config.treeFarmReach.tool: How far from their Chopping Block, in blocks, a lumberjack takes a tree farm outside the village. Anywhere in the village the block stands in is always in reach.
aliveworkplace.config.orchardAreaReach.t: How far from their workstation, in blocks, an orchard keeper takes a marked orchard outside the village. Anywhere in the village the workstation stands in is always in reach.
aliveworkplace.config.berryPlotReach.too: How far from their workstation, in blocks, a berry breeder takes a berry plot outside the village. Anywhere in the village the workstation stands in is always in reach.
aliveworkplace.config.guardRadius.toolti: How far from their Grindstone, in blocks, guards patrol and fight.
aliveworkplace.config.lumberjackRadius.t: How far from their Fletching Table, in blocks, lumberjacks cut trees.
aliveworkplace.config.orchardRadius.tool: How far from their Composter, in blocks, orchard keepers pick fruit.
aliveworkplace.config.fisherRadius.toolt: How far from their workstation, in blocks, fishermen look for water to fish in.
aliveworkplace.config.explorerRange.tool: How far from their Cartography Table, in blocks, explorers go on an expedition.
aliveworkplace.config.partnerRadius.tool: How far from a workstation, in blocks, pastured Pokémon count as a worker's partners (with Cobblemon).
aliveworkplace.config.postmanRange.toolt: How far from their Mailbox, in blocks, a postman walks to deliver. Farther mail arrives at dawn.
aliveworkplace.config.maxWorkersPerVilla: Jobless villagers stop taking free workstations once this many workstations in their village are taken. Nobody loses a job they have. 0: no limit.
A jobless villager who takes a block several jobs share (a composter, a lectern, a Shop Counter...) by themselves gets one of its jobs at random, likelier the fewer of it the village has. Off: always the block's vanilla job.
aliveworkplace.config.minerCraftsPickaxe: A Miner whose pickaxe wore out, or who has none, makes a new one at their workstation from what they mined: stone, then iron from Journeyman and diamond from Expert. Off: they wait for a pickaxe from you or the Toolsmith.
aliveworkplace.config.villageWaystones.t: With Waystones installed, the Steward proposes a waystone plaza by the Village Hall, its waystone named after the village. Off: the plaza isn't proposed; stones already standing stay. Without Waystones it does nothing.
aliveworkplace.config.quarryBuild.toolti: The Quarry blueprint: the Miner at its blast furnace digs its pit without a Quarry Marker, and what they dig grows back slowly (mostly stone, some coal and copper, rarely iron, gold, redstone and diamond). Off: the Quarry isn't offered and nothing grows back; the Quarry Marker works as before.
aliveworkplace.config.quarryRegrowth.too: How many blocks grow back in a Quarry's pit in a Minecraft day (0: none). At 100, a pit dug out to the bottom takes about a week to fill up again.
aliveworkplace.config.fishermanCap.toolt: Builds are full of storage barrels, a fisherman's workstation. On: a village takes only so many fishermen, and other jobless villagers pass free barrels by for another workstation. A fisherman a village already has keeps his job.
aliveworkplace.config.fishermenPerVillag: With the Fisherman Cap on, how many fishermen every village takes, however small.
aliveworkplace.config.villagersPerFisher: With the Fisherman Cap on, a village takes one more fisherman for every this many villagers in it.
aliveworkplace.config.workerPathRange.to: How far villagers with a job look for a path in one go, in blocks. Lower is lighter on the server: farther walks are made in legs. Vanilla: 48.
aliveworkplace.config.villageRadius.tool: Workers whose workstations are this many blocks apart or closer are one village and share their chests. 0: every worker keeps to their own chests.
How far from a Village Hall, in blocks, its village reaches.
aliveworkplace.config.builderPaths.toolt: Builders lay a dirt path from each finished building to the village's bell or Village Hall.
aliveworkplace.config.keepVillagesWorkin: Villages keep working when no player is near: while anyone is online, each worker's workstation stays loaded. Off: villages nobody is near pause.
aliveworkplace.config.villageGrowthCap.t: A village with a Village Hall stops having babies at this many villagers. 0: villages don't grow.
aliveworkplace.config.villagerNames.tool: Villagers in a village with a Village Hall get names.
aliveworkplace.config.villagerTraits.too: Villagers have traits (diligent, lazy, nimble...) that change how they work.
aliveworkplace.config.villagerSickness.t: Villagers in a village with a Village Hall fall ill now and then; a Nurse cures them.
aliveworkplace.config.villagerMoods.tool: Villagers in a village with a Village Hall have moods that change how fast they work.
aliveworkplace.config.legends.tooltip: Rare named villagers with powers can come to villages that earn them. Off: none come, and those already settled stay as ordinary Masters of their trade.
aliveworkplace.config.legendNeeds.toolti: A settled Legend needs a home of their own (tier III or better), their luxury once a week and a happy village, and goes on strike without them. Off: no needs are checked and strikes end.
message.aliveworkplace.legend.off: Legends are switched off (legends in the config).

message.aliveworkplace.legend.mythic.set: A Mythic Legend! %s, the %s, has settled in %s, %s blocks %s of spawn.
message.aliveworkplace.legend.mythic.gue: A Mythic Legend! %s, the %s, has come to %s as a guest, %s blocks %s of spawn.

message.aliveworkplace.legend.refused.le: The %s already lives in this world: a Legendary Legend comes once to each world.

A %s can hold %s Mythic Legend, and this one has %s.

chronicle.aliveworkplace.legend.guest: %s, the %s (a %s Legend), came to the village as a guest
chronicle.aliveworkplace.legend.joined: %s, the %s, joined the village's new hall
chronicle.aliveworkplace.legend.strike_o: %s, the %s, has all they asked for and went back to work
chronicle.aliveworkplace.legend.grand_up: %s, the %s, asked for the %s to be upgraded, and %s took it on
chronicle.aliveworkplace.legend.grand_re: %s, the %s, redrew the %s in the Grand style, and %s took it on
chronicle.aliveworkplace.legend.grand_st: %s, the %s, went on strike, and the work on the %s stopped
legend.aliveworkplace.power.grand_rebuil: Every %s days, a building the builders finished is upgraded, or redrawn in the %s style
message.aliveworkplace.legend.grand_paus: %s will leave the village's buildings as they are
message.aliveworkplace.legend.grand_resu: %s will make the village's buildings grander again
legend.aliveworkplace.master_architect.l: Halls for kings, bridges for cities, a lighthouse no storm has moved: all drawn by one hand. A town that builds in many styles is worth a visit, and worth making grand.
legend.aliveworkplace.pathfinder.title: Pathfinder
legend.aliveworkplace.pathfinder.lore: There is no road they haven't walked, and few they didn't walk first. Somewhere under the hills a stronghold sleeps, a city of echoes waits, and they know the way to both.
legend.aliveworkplace.old_sage.title: Old Sage
legend.aliveworkplace.old_sage.lore: They have lived alone with their books so long that the forest forgot them. They remember the old tongues, the star charts and the herb lore, and they will teach a village that earns it, once it has answered their riddles.
legend.aliveworkplace.seer.title: Seer
legend.aliveworkplace.seer.lore: They came out of the moonlight one night and knelt in the Chapel as if they had always known the way. They read tomorrow in the stars as others read a ledger, and they are never wrong.
legend.aliveworkplace.power.foretell: Foretells at dawn: whether raiders come that night and from which side, the next festival and market day, and the next day's guest; warns of attacks %s days ahead
legend.aliveworkplace.power.bless_weddin: Blesses weddings at the Chapel: the couple is %s happier for %s days, and their first baby comes within %s days when a bed is free
message.aliveworkplace.seer.dawn: At dawn %s looks to the fading stars and foretells for %s:
message.aliveworkplace.seer.raid: Raiders will come tonight, from the %s.
message.aliveworkplace.seer.no_market: No market day: the village has no Market Square.
message.aliveworkplace.seer.blessed: %s blessed the wedding of %s and %s: may they be happy, and may a child come soon
chronicle.aliveworkplace.blessed_wedding: %s blessed the wedding of %s and %s at the Chapel
message.aliveworkplace.wonder.wedding_bl: The bells of the %3$s ring out: %1$s and %2$s are wed at its altar, and the wedding is blessed. All of %4$s is %5$s happier for %6$s days
chronicle.aliveworkplace.wonder_wedding: %s and %s were wed at the altar of the %s, and the wedding was blessed
advice.aliveworkplace.seer_raid: The Seer foretells raiders tonight, from the %s
advice.aliveworkplace.seer_raid.how: Post guards on the %s side and see everyone home before dark.
advice.aliveworkplace.seer_calm: The Seer foretells a quiet night
advice.aliveworkplace.seer_days.how: As the Seer foretold at dawn. Stock the store for the feast and have goods ready for the traders.
advice.aliveworkplace.seer_guest.how: The %s will come to %s. Have a free bed in a tier III home and their luxury ready, so they stay.
advice.aliveworkplace.seer_no_guest.how: So the Seer foretold at dawn.
legend.aliveworkplace.merchant_prince.lo: Their fleet went down with every coin they had, and they came ashore with nothing but a crimson coat and a head for numbers. Feed them, and they will make a rich village richer: a bank in the hall, fairs in the square and fair prices on every road.
legend.aliveworkplace.grand_chef.title: Grand Chef
legend.aliveworkplace.grand_chef.lore: A chef who cooked for a week without sleeping and came out of the kitchen with a cake the whole village still talks about. Their banquets fill the tables, the hearts and, before long, the cradles.
legend.aliveworkplace.power.banquet: Every %s days a banquet: %s meals each from the store, everyone who comes %s happier for %s days, and babies twice as often for %s days
message.aliveworkplace.banquet.call: The Grand Chef calls %s to a banquet tonight!
message.aliveworkplace.banquet.feast: The banquet in %s: %s kinds of meal on the tables

legend.aliveworkplace.bard_laureate.lore: A bard who sang at a festival so loud and so long that the whole crowd learned the tune by heart. They write every village they love a song of its own, and the fields go quicker when they sing.
legend.aliveworkplace.bard_laureate.name: Ollamh
Rosalind
Taliesin
legend.aliveworkplace.power.anthem: Composes the village's anthem from its name, played at every festival, rank-up, wedding and Legend arrival
legend.aliveworkplace.power.work_songs: Twice a day sings for %s minutes where work is busiest: workers within %s blocks work %s× as fast, everyone who hears is %s happier for the day
A scholar who has walked every route and filled three notebooks on a single Pidgey. Show them your partners and they'll tell you what each one was born good at; let them stay, and every Pokémon the village keeps goes in their Pokédex.
legend.aliveworkplace.power.pokemon_hint: Right-click them with an empty hand: each of your party's IVs in words, the stats its nature raises and lowers, whether it has its hidden ability, and its EVs
legend.aliveworkplace.power.pokedex: Logs every species kept in the village's pastures in the hall's Pokédex, which opens the topics of the Pokédex research

legend.aliveworkplace.pokemon_ranger.lor: A wanderer of the wild routes with a capture styler on the wrist, who follows the giants of the land. Where an Alpha roams near a village, the Ranger comes to calm it; let them stay, and wild Pokémon follow them home to the village's pastures.
legend.aliveworkplace.power.calm_alphas: Each morning walks to an Alpha Pokémon within 96 blocks of the hall and calms it: it never again attacks villagers or players in the village
legend.aliveworkplace.power.befriend: Once a day befriends a wild Pokémon within 64 blocks (never a legendary, mythical, Ultra Beast or paradox one) and leads it to a village Pasture Block with room, as the hall owner's Pokémon
rule.aliveworkplace.alpha_near: An Alpha Pokémon (or a wild one of level 50 or more) within %3$s blocks of the hall: %1$s of %2$s

legend.aliveworkplace.beastmaster.title: Beastmaster
legend.aliveworkplace.beastmaster.lore: A rancher the pillagers caught and kept in a cage for a season, who talked their own wolves round through the bars. Every guard of theirs walks with a war dog at heel, and the horses they breed outrun the wind.
legend.aliveworkplace.power.war_dogs: Tames a war dog for every guard with %s bones from their chest, in wolf armor from %s armadillo scutes; it follows its guard and fights what they fight, and a lost dog is replaced after %s days
legend.aliveworkplace.power.horse_breedi: Breeds the ranch's best horses with golden carrots, up to %s: each foal gets the best speed, jump and health of its parents and a little more, and guards ride them first

screen.aliveworkplace.anthem.about: Played at every festival, rank-up, wedding and Legend arrival
screen.aliveworkplace.anthem.play_hint: Rings out over the hall for everyone near
legend.aliveworkplace.power.bank: The treasury earns %s%% a day on what it holds, and holds %s times as much
legend.aliveworkplace.power.trade_fair: Every %s days a trade fair: %s traders and a stall for each village we trade with, every trade %s%% cheaper
legend.aliveworkplace.power.keeps_to: By day they keep to the Village Hall and the Market Square
legend.aliveworkplace.power.caravan_pay: Every stack our caravans bring to a village that was waiting for it earns the treasury %s emerald
legend.aliveworkplace.golem_smith.title: Golem Smith
legend.aliveworkplace.golem_smith.lore: A tinkerer who stopped mending golems and started making them. Give them iron and a smithing table, and the village will never lack strong hands again.
legend.aliveworkplace.power.golem_forge: Builds a golem every %s days from the chests by their smithing table, up to one per %s villagers; sneak-right-click them to choose which comes next. Mends golems twice as fast as a Tinkerer
message.aliveworkplace.golem_smith.cost: 4 iron blocks, a carved pumpkin and 1 %s in the chests by their smithing table
message.aliveworkplace.sage.rumour: A rumor reaches %3$s: an old hermit lives alone in a hut about %1$s blocks to the %2$s. They say the hermit knows the old lore.
message.aliveworkplace.sage.riddle.1: I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, rivers but no water. What am I?
message.aliveworkplace.sage.riddle.2: I point the way but never walk. What am I?
message.aliveworkplace.sage.riddle.3: I follow the sun all day but never see the sky. What am I?
message.aliveworkplace.sage.riddle.4: I have a spine but no bones, and leaves but no branches. What am I?
message.aliveworkplace.sage.riddle.5: I'm full of holes, yet I hold water. What am I?
message.aliveworkplace.sage.riddle.6: Feed me and I live; give me a drink and I die. What am I?
message.aliveworkplace.sage.riddle.7: I run but never walk, and have a bed but never sleep. What am I?
message.aliveworkplace.sage.riddle.8: I sleep under the mountains until a pick wakes me, and then every villager wants me. What am I?
message.aliveworkplace.sage.wrong: %s looks at the %s and shakes their head.
message.aliveworkplace.sage.hint.1: explorers draw me as they walk.
message.aliveworkplace.sage.hint.2: my needle is red and very stubborn.
message.aliveworkplace.sage.hint.3: gold and redstone keep my time.
message.aliveworkplace.sage.hint.4: leather and paper make me, and scholars love me.
message.aliveworkplace.sage.hint.5: the guardians of the ocean temples keep me.
message.aliveworkplace.sage.hint.6: a stick and a lump of coal.
message.aliveworkplace.sage.hint.7: iron carries me home from the river.
message.aliveworkplace.sage.hint.8: green, and every trader counts in me.
message.aliveworkplace.legend_site.thank: %s: "Three for three! It has been an age since anyone was worth teaching. Expect me at %s's hall in the morning."
chronicle.aliveworkplace.iron_pact: An iron golem came to keep the Iron Pact
research.aliveworkplace.ancient_lore.old: Inn travelers are Journeymen at least, and Gifted twice as often
research.aliveworkplace.ancient_lore.sta: Explorers range 25% farther a level, and at II draw a map every second expedition
research.aliveworkplace.ancient_lore.her: Illness lasts a day less a level, and nurses also cure with any small flower
research.aliveworkplace.ancient_lore.dee: Every villager learns 15% faster a level
research.aliveworkplace.ancient_lore.run: Night raids are 20% less likely a level

screen.aliveworkplace.legends.grave: In their grave: an Undertaker can bring them back

screen.aliveworkplace.legends.ready: This village has all they need: they may come
advice.aliveworkplace.legend.how: Only one thing is missing for the %s: %s. The Legends page says how they come.
chatter.aliveworkplace.legend_here.0: We have a Legend among us: %s!
chatter.aliveworkplace.legend_here.1: Have you met %s? The whole village is proud.
chatter.aliveworkplace.legend_guest.0: %s is staying with us! Do you think they'll settle?
chatter.aliveworkplace.legend_guest.1: A Legend as our guest: %s. Let's give them everything they need.
chatter.aliveworkplace.legend_strike.0: %s has downed tools. They won't work till they get what they want.
chatter.aliveworkplace.legend_self.0: Yes, I am the %s. Don't let it go to your head; I try not to.
chatter.aliveworkplace.edict_long_shifts: Work till the lamps go out, they say. Every day, they say.
Free bread at the hall! I could get used to this.
The bread's free, but the granary empties fast.
chatter.aliveworkplace.edict_large_famil: Babies everywhere. Somebody has to feed them all.
Big families are lovely, but half of them have a cough.
So many new faces since the gates opened!
Open gates let in guests... and bandits, I hear.
chatter.aliveworkplace.edict_festival_se: Another festival soon! The treasury had better hold.
Festival Season! I've barely put the bunting away.
chatter.aliveworkplace.edict_tithe.0: A tenth of everything to the hall. The prices went up too.
chatter.aliveworkplace.edict_tithe.1: The tithe fills the treasury. Not my purse, mind.
chatter.aliveworkplace.edict_curfew.0: Home by dark, or the watch scolds us.
chatter.aliveworkplace.edict_curfew.1: Curfew's safe, I grant you. Dull, but safe.
chatter.aliveworkplace.edict_conscriptio: I've a sword now, and no idea how to hold it.
If the raiders come, we all drop our tools and fight.
chatter.aliveworkplace.reformed_long_shi: The shift bell's rung. Home we go.
Long days, but the bell tells us when to stop. Fair enough.
chatter.aliveworkplace.reformed_free_bre: The Common Granary keeps the bread coming and the stores full.
Free bread, and nobody goes short. That's a good law.
chatter.aliveworkplace.reformed_large_fa: The midwives keep the little ones well. Bless them.
Big families, and hardly a sniffle since the midwives came.
chatter.aliveworkplace.reformed_open_gat: Guests come in, and the watch keeps the bandits out.
With the Watchful Gate, I sleep easy with the gates open.
chatter.aliveworkplace.reformed_festival: The Festival Fund pays for every party. Wonderful!
Festivals galore, and the treasury doesn't even blink.
chatter.aliveworkplace.reformed_tithe.0: The Fair Ledger keeps the tithe honest, and prices fair.
chatter.aliveworkplace.reformed_tithe.1: I don't mind the tithe now the books are open.
chatter.aliveworkplace.reformed_curfew.0: The lamplighters keep the streets bright. No more hiding indoors.
chatter.aliveworkplace.reformed_curfew.1: Safe nights, and I can still take an evening stroll.
chatter.aliveworkplace.reformed_conscrip: We drilled all winter. Now only those near the fight drop their tools.
The militia knows its drill. The rest of us keep working.
chatter.aliveworkplace.rush.0: The horn's blown! Faster, everyone, faster!
chatter.aliveworkplace.rush.1: A rush today. I'll be worn out by tonight.
chatter.aliveworkplace.tonic.0: That %s put a spring in my step!
chatter.aliveworkplace.tonic.1: One sip of %s and I could work all day.
chatter.aliveworkplace.guild.0: Proud to be one of the %s.
chatter.aliveworkplace.guild.1: The %s look after their own. Better tools, better pay.
chatter.aliveworkplace.class_rose.0: We've come up in the world, and the whole village knows it.
chatter.aliveworkplace.class_rose.1: Folk nod to us in the square now. We earned that.
chatter.aliveworkplace.class_rose.2: New standing, same hands. Still, it feels good.
chatter.aliveworkplace.class_fell.0: We've come down in the world. Don't look at me like that.
chatter.aliveworkplace.class_fell.1: Hard times. We'll climb back, you'll see.
chatter.aliveworkplace.class_fell.2: Fewer friends at the well since we came down.
A cup of wine with supper, that's all I ask. The store's dry.
Folk of our standing drink wine. If only there were any to be had.
Is there a vintner in this village or not? I could do with a glass.
chatter.aliveworkplace.class_wants_cloth: Look at these rags. I need something new to wear.
Everyone notices clothes, and mine have seen better days.
If the tailor has anything new, I'd wear it gladly.
chatter.aliveworkplace.gazette_news.0: Did you read the Gazette? The whole village is in it this week.
chatter.aliveworkplace.gazette_news.1: I read every word of the Gazette. Nothing gets past me now.
chatter.aliveworkplace.gazette_news.2: The Gazette says we're doing well. I believe it.
chatter.aliveworkplace.tavern_glad.0: Thank goodness for the tavern. A warm fire and good company.
chatter.aliveworkplace.tavern_glad.1: I'll be at the tavern tonight, if anyone's asking.
chatter.aliveworkplace.tavern_glad.2: A village with a tavern is a village worth living in.
chatter.aliveworkplace.colours.0: Have you seen our banner? Those are our colors.
chatter.aliveworkplace.colours.1: Our colors fly over the hall. Makes a village feel like home.
advice.aliveworkplace.edict_slot.how: Edicts a %2$s may still put in force: %1$s. Proclaim one on the hall's Edicts page: each gives the village a boost at a cost.
advice.aliveworkplace.reform_step.how: %s waits on the Quests page: %s. Finish every step and the edict loses its cost.
advice.aliveworkplace.festival_fund: The treasury can't pay for the next festival (%s of %s emeralds)
advice.aliveworkplace.festival_fund.how: Festival Season makes every festival cost emeralds. Fill the treasury (taxes, the tithe, the market), or the festival is called off and the villagers are disappointed.
advice.aliveworkplace.guildhall.how: A chartered guild gives no perks until a builder finishes a Guildhall in the village. Give a builder the Guildhall blueprint.
advice.aliveworkplace.cradle.how: Put a Cradle near a bed: children grow up faster there, sleep in it at night, and the village may have an extra baby a day.
advice.aliveworkplace.harvest_idol: Harvest season, and no Harvest Idol by the fields
advice.aliveworkplace.harvest_idol.how: In autumn a Harvest Idol makes the crops within 32 blocks of it grow faster. Set one near the fields round the hall.
aliveworkplace.config.builderRepairs.too: Idle builders repair the buildings they finished when blocks go missing. Off: they still put back what raiders and village fires took.
aliveworkplace.config.repairAsk.tooltip: A builder who finds blocks missing from a finished build asks first (Repair it? Yes / Not now, in chat and on the Village Hall's Repairs page) and repairs only what you agreed to. Off: they repair by themselves, as before. What raiders and village fires took is always repaired without asking.
aliveworkplace.config.marketDays.tooltip: A village with a Village Hall and a Market Square holds a market once a week.
aliveworkplace.config.villageRaids.toolt: Monsters raid bigger villages with a Village Hall at night now and then.
aliveworkplace.config.banditCamps.toolti: Bandits make camp near villages of Village rank or more now and then, and raid them until their chief falls.
aliveworkplace.config.sieges.tooltip: A raid by raiders who ram gates on a village with a finished wall or gate is a siege: the gates shut, the portcullis drops and the rams go for the gate. Off: every raid is a plain one.
aliveworkplace.config.threatLevel.toolti: How hard the village's threats are, beside each one's own switch. 0: none at all (no raids, raiders' camps, sieges or disasters). 1, gentle: half as often, no sieges (raiders walk in), no hexes, no plague. 2: normal. 3, hard: half again as often, and a quarter more raiders. On Peaceful nothing comes.
A raider, bandit or camp mob another mod refuses to spawn (a mob blocklist such as MobsBeGone, which Cobbleverse ships with pillagers and zombies on it) is put in the world anyway, so camps and raids aren't empty. Off: such mobs are left out, and the server log says which.
aliveworkplace.config.forceVillageSpawns: The village's own iron golems, relief riders' horses, the Beastmaster's foals and wolf pups and a caravan's pack llamas are put in the world even when another mod refuses them (a mob blocklist such as MobsBeGone, which Cobbleverse ships with golems, wolves, horses and llamas on it). Off: they are left out, and the server log says which. Animals the game spawns by itself are never forced.
aliveworkplace.config.campRuins.tooltip: A bandit camp or other raiders' camp whose captain is killed (or that leaves the village in peace) stays as ruins with its fire put out. Off: the camp is taken down a few seconds later, and the loot in its chests spills out on the ground.
aliveworkplace.config.siegeDamage.toolti: In a siege, rams break only the gate blocks of finished walls and gates, and a village fire can burn the builders' blocks; builders always put back what either took. No other raider breaks a builder's block. Off: gates hold and fires burn nothing. The mobGriefing gamerule off holds the gates too.
aliveworkplace.config.festivals.tooltip: Villages with a Village Hall hold a festival every season. Players can still call one with a cake.
aliveworkplace.config.nurseHealingMachin: A nurse working at Cobblemon's Healing Machine puts your team in it to heal them (free), and keeps it charged while she's on shift. Off: she heals your team by hand, as at any station.
aliveworkplace.config.berryBreeders.tool: With Cobblemon: sneak-right-click a villager by a composter with any berry and she breeds new berries from the village's own, planting the parent pairs side by side. Off: no Berry Breeder job, and breeders already hired stand idle.
aliveworkplace.config.campCooks.tooltip: With Cobblemon: sneak-right-click a villager by a Campfire Pot with Hearty Grains and she cooks Cobblemon dishes in the pot from the chest beside it. Off: no Camp Cook job, and cooks already hired stand idle.
aliveworkplace.config.habitatKeepers.too: With Cobblemon: sneak-right-click a villager by a Pasture Block with a honey bottle and she keeps the wild Pokémon round it, with snacks set out and Saccharine logs slathered with honey. Off: no Habitat Keeper job, and keepers already hired stand idle.
aliveworkplace.config.vintners.tooltip: Sneak-right-click a villager by a cauldron with sweet berries, glow berries or an apple and they press Cider, Berry Wine and Vintage Wine for the village store. Off: no Vintner job, and Vintners already hired stand idle.
aliveworkplace.config.tailors.tooltip: Sneak-right-click a villager by a loom with string and they sew Work Clothes, Fine Clothes and Noble Robes for the village store. Off: no Tailor job, and Tailors already hired stand idle.
aliveworkplace.config.jewellers.tooltip: Sneak-right-click a villager by a stonecutter with a gold nugget and they make Amethyst Rings, Emerald Brooches and Gold Circlets for the village store. Off: no Jeweler job, and Jewelers already hired stand idle.
aliveworkplace.config.printers.tooltip: Sneak-right-click a villager by a cartography table with an ink sac and they print books, the Village Gazette and Illuminated Books for the village store. Off: no Printer job, Printers already hired stand idle, and no Spread the news quest goes up.
aliveworkplace.config.gemGrowers.tooltip: Sneak-right-click a villager by a stonecutter with an amethyst shard and she tends the gem beds round it: amethyst, and with Cobblemon tumblestones and Type Gems. Off: no Gem Grower job, and growers already hired stand idle.
aliveworkplace.config.daycareKeepers.too: Sneak-right-click a villager by a Pasture Block with an egg and she keeps one pair of Pokémon per player, finding their eggs at dawn (with Cobblemon). Off: no Daycare Keeper job, and keepers already hired find no eggs.
aliveworkplace.config.habitatSightings.t: Habitat Keepers tell the village of the shiny, rare and Alpha wild Pokémon they spot near their pasture, and write them in the chronicle. Off: they keep their sightings to themselves.
aliveworkplace.config.villageHabitats.to: With Cobblemon 1.8, an Expert Habitat Keeper puts one Habitat Block under the center stone of a finished Habitat Garden, with Pokémon that suit the biome. One per village; taking the garden down removes it. Off: no village gets one.
aliveworkplace.config.pokemonVillageHous: With Cobblemon, villages sometimes grow a Pokémon Center, a Camp Kitchen, a Berry Nursery, a Daycare and a Gem Grotto, each with its worker already in the job. Off: new villages don't grow them (from the next server start).
aliveworkplace.config.festivalCup.toolti: With Cobblemon, a village with a hall, a finished Arena and at least Village rank holds its festivals as a Festival Cup for the Trainers of its trade partners and the players who sign up on the hall's Cup page. Off: no Cups; festivals stay plain.
Which of a host village's festivals are Cups: 1 makes every festival a Cup, 2 every second one, and so on.
aliveworkplace.config.partnerShows.toolt: Pokémon pastured near a workstation are seen helping: they walk over to the work, carry things and lend a hand (with Cobblemon).
aliveworkplace.config.villagerChatter.to: Villagers near a player now and then say something about their day, over their heads.
aliveworkplace.config.villagerCouples.to: Villagers court, marry (a wedding at the bell) and mourn.
aliveworkplace.config.villageTreasury.to: Villages with a Village Hall put by takings every morning for players to collect at the hall.
aliveworkplace.config.villageQuests.tool: Village Halls post quests for players each morning. Off: no new quests go up; open ones can still be finished.
aliveworkplace.config.questbookKeepEdits: With FTB Quests: on, the questbook chapters already on the server are kept as they are when the mod brings new versions (new chapters still come in). Off: each start brings the new version of every chapter; a chapter you deleted stays deleted.
aliveworkplace.config.blueprintUnlocks.t: On, the Blueprint Table is a collection: each village starts with the basics and unlocks the rest by buying blueprints, its builders' level-ups, questbook rewards and blueprints found in chests. Off: every build is in the Table, as before.
aliveworkplace.config.friendship.tooltip: Named villagers keep a friendship with each player, ten hearts shown when you look at them: trades, quests, help in a fight and weddings raise it, hitting them lowers it. Off: no points and no hearts shown; friendships stay saved.

gift.aliveworkplace.refuse.day: You already gave me something today, %s. Keep it for tomorrow.
gift.aliveworkplace.refuse.week: Two gifts in one week is plenty, %s. Keep it for next week.
gift.aliveworkplace.liked.1: Oh, %1$s. I do like that. Thank you!
gift.aliveworkplace.disliked.1: Hm. %1$s. I'll find somewhere to put it.
gift.aliveworkplace.hated.1: Ugh, %1$s. Take it as a hint, %2$s: never again.
gift.aliveworkplace.name_day: %s And on my name day, too!
screen.aliveworkplace.hall.name_day.toda: Name day: today (a gift counts three times)
aliveworkplace.config.storyArcs.tooltip: Now and then a village lives through a story told in chapters over several days. Off: no story starts, and one running ends quietly at its next round.
aliveworkplace.config.arcCooldownDays.to: Days a village rests between two stories (and before its first).
aliveworkplace.config.arcsAtOnce.tooltip: How many stories may run at once on the whole server. 0: none.
One caravan in this many on a road over 300 blocks goes missing, starting the Lost Caravan story. 0: none.
A Village Hall's owner may protect the village from other players (a setting on the hall, off until they turn it on).
aliveworkplace.config.maxWorkPace.toolti: How fast all the bonuses together (Pokémon partners, a well-kept village, research, traits, a happy mood, edicts) can make a worker, in percent of the usual pace: 200 is twice as fast. Sickness and bad moods still slow them after that; a worker's level doesn't count.
aliveworkplace.config.villageEdicts.tool: A village's owner may proclaim edicts at the Village Hall: laws with a boost and a cost, such as Long Shifts. Off: none can be proclaimed and those in force do nothing, but they stay saved and come back when it's on.
aliveworkplace.config.villageBanners.too: A Village Banner (any banner and a gold ingot) right-clicked on a Village Hall makes its design the village's colors. Off: none can be crafted or set; colors already set stay saved.
tooltip.aliveworkplace.village_banner.hi: Right-click a Village Hall to make this the village's colors
message.aliveworkplace.village_banner.se: These are now the colors of %s

screen.aliveworkplace.edicts.banner_show: Over the doors of new buildings, on the guards' shields, at festivals and on the caravans' routes
screen.aliveworkplace.edicts.banner_chan: Right-click the hall with another Village Banner to change them
screen.aliveworkplace.edicts.banner_how: Right-click the hall with a Village Banner (any banner and a gold ingot) to give the village its colors
aliveworkplace.config.workHorns.tooltip: A Work Horn blown in a village calls a rush: its villagers work 50% faster for 5 minutes, once a day, then are worn out until dawn. Off: the horn only sounds.
aliveworkplace.config.edictMinDays.toolt: Days an edict stays in force before it can be lifted.
aliveworkplace.config.seasonDays.tooltip: Days in each of the village calendar's four seasons. Each season has a festival on its middle day.
What each worker brings the village treasury a day, in hundredths of an emerald, before wellbeing and rank.
What an emerald price comes to in CobbleDollars: lessons, shops and fares (with CobbleDollars).

aliveworkplace.config.stewardSelfRun.too: A Steward set to Run the village starts the builds he proposes by himself and tells the hall's owner each morning. Off: every village asks first.
aliveworkplace.config.stewardRoads.toolt: A Steward's builders build the approved roads on the City Plan, a segment of up to 24 blocks at a time when no building waits, and every new building's door joins the nearest road with a lane. Off: roads are drawn on the plan but not built.
aliveworkplace.config.caravanRoads.toolt: Two villages with a trade route each build their half of a street to the other, from the end of their nearest road, while their Steward's builders are free. The halves meet halfway; a half that can't reach that far ends at a milestone naming the other village. Caravans on a finished road arrive in three quarters of the time. Only loaded land is planned. Off: no roads between villages.
aliveworkplace.config.caravanRoadReach.t: The longest half of a road, in blocks, a village builds towards another (it goes halfway at most). Two halves that would end within 32 blocks of each other are carried on to meet.

aliveworkplace.config.legendSites.toolti: A Legend may wait at a ruined portal (a traveler's camp), a pillager outpost (a prisoner in a cage) or a shipwreck (a castaway on the beach) for a player whose village has earned them. Off: no camps, and no structure lookups at all.
aliveworkplace.config.strangeMoods.toolt: Once a day a Master in a happy village may be taken by a strange mood: they claim their workstation and ask for three rare materials within 3 days. Brought, they make a named Masterwork and become a Legend; not, they sulk for a week. Off: no strange moods, and a mood already on is called off.
message.aliveworkplace.legend_site.found: Beside the ruined portal, a traveler has made camp: %s. Talk to them.
At the foot of the outpost's tower, a prisoner rattles an iron cage: %s. Break the bars to free them.
On the beach near the wreck, a castaway has made camp: %s. They look starved: bring them a cooked meal.
message.aliveworkplace.legend_site.thank: %s: "Well met! I've heard of %s. I'll be at your Village Hall in the morning."
%s: "Free at last, thank you! I'll find my way to %s and be at your hall by morning."
%s: "A hot meal, at last! I owe you my life. Look for me at %s's hall in the morning."

aliveworkplace.config.realms.tooltip: A Town can found a realm on its hall's Realm tab and add its owner's other villages. Off: no Realm tab; realms stay saved and come back.
aliveworkplace.config.realmMaxMembers.to: How many villages one realm may hold.
aliveworkplace.config.realmRelief.toolti: When a realm village is raided, the capital and members within 1,024 blocks send riders to help, an emerald each from the realm treasury. Off: nobody comes.
aliveworkplace.config.tradePacts.tooltip: A caravan route to another player's village needs a trade pact, offered and accepted on the hall's Pacts tab. Pact caravans are paid for what they bring. Off: routes need no pact.
aliveworkplace.config.alliances.tooltip: Villages of different owners can ally. Allies within 1,024 blocks send relief riders to each other's raids. Off: no alliances are offered and no riders come.
aliveworkplace.config.feuds.tooltip: An owner can declare a feud on another player's village or realm on the Pacts tab. Pacts and caravans between them end, and each board pays the rival's people 25% less and charges them 25% more. Peace by letter, or it fades after 7 days. Off: no feuds.
aliveworkplace.config.feudWars.tooltip: With PvP on, a feud can become a war of up to 3 days: each side's guards fight the other side's owners inside their own village. Blocks, chests, villagers and treasuries stay protected. Off: no wars.
aliveworkplace.config.realmMap.tooltip: A member's Realm tab draws the realm on an empty map: a banner for every member in the realm's color, colonies, allies and rivals in their own, and the caravan routes as dotted lines. Off: no map button.
Once a week everyone online hears how the villages did: the Biggest, the Richest, the Happiest, Most Legends and the Greatest realm. Owners can leave their village off on the Trade page. Off: nothing is counted or announced.
aliveworkplace.config.leaderboardHour.to: The hour, server time, the weekly leaderboard is read out (the day is leaderboardDay in the file, Sunday by default).

guild.aliveworkplace.builders.perk: Builders, Carpenters, Masons and Dyers work 15% faster; up to 5 idle builders help at a build (not 3).

guild.aliveworkplace.healers.perk: Nurses, Clerics and Undertakers work 15% faster; the village's ill get well in two days (not three), and nurses and undertakers look 48 blocks out (not 32).
guild.aliveworkplace.merchants.perk: Shopkeepers, Innkeepers, Ferrymen, Postmen and Porters work 15% faster; travelers cost a quarter less to hire, and porters carry 3 more stacks.
guild.aliveworkplace.wardens.perk: Guards train on the dummies up to Master (not Expert) and hit 10% harder.
guild.aliveworkplace.trainers.perk: Move Tutors' lessons and Fossil Scientists' revivals cost a fifth less, and Trainers and Trainer Leaders rank up a quarter faster.

message.aliveworkplace.evergreen.no_trai: %1$s won't take it. The charm is for an elder who is a Master of their trade, Gifted, a Legend, or happy (mood %2$s or more) for %3$s days running. Happy days so far: %4$s.

aliveworkplace.config.villageMourning.to: When a villager dies the village is told who it was, their job and years, their family grieve for 3 days (lower mood, slower work), and the Undertaker leads a funeral at the grave. Off: none of it (a partner still mourns).

message.aliveworkplace.elder.passed_char: %s, an elder, passed away in the night. An Undertaker can bring them back, and an Evergreen Charm keeps an elder for good.

chatter.aliveworkplace.elder.1: I've seen more harvests than you've had hot dinners.
chatter.aliveworkplace.elder.2: These knees knew every path in the village, once.
chatter.aliveworkplace.elder.3: Sit a while. The young ones are always in a hurry.

aliveworkplace.config.villagerAges.toolt: Grown villagers count their days and become elders. Off: nobody is an elder, so nobody passes away of old age; the day each grew up stays saved.
Days a villager has been grown up before they are an elder.
aliveworkplace.config.elderPassing.toolt: An elder passes away in the night after 400 elder days and leaves a grave (an Undertaker can bring them back; an Evergreen Charm keeps them for good). Off: elders never die of old age.
The Undertaker moves each grave lying about the village (a street, a field, a doorstep) to the village's Graveyard, in rows, and still brings villagers back from there. A village without a Graveyard gets a small plot near the hall. Off: graves stay where villagers fall.
aliveworkplace.config.agelessElders.tool: Sneak-right-click an elder with an Evergreen Charm and, if they are a Master, Gifted, a Legend or have been happy for 20 days, they become ageless. Off: charms are refused; elders already ageless stay so.
aliveworkplace.config.classOutfits.toolt: Villagers wear their class over their job's outfit (an Artisan's neckerchief, a Burgher's collar and watch chain, a Noble's mantle), and elders have gray brows and a beard. Off: only the job's outfit is drawn.
aliveworkplace.config.elderRetirement.to: An elder with a job retires once a jobless villager can take over (one a village every 3 days): the successor learns from them for 2 days, then takes the workstation, the job one level below and its fields and routes. Retired elders mentor Novices and Apprentices of their old trade, who learn 50% faster. Off: nobody starts retiring.
aliveworkplace.config.familyNames.toolti: Every villager in a village with a hall has a family name, shown on the hall ("Dara (Ashby)") and in the chronicle; children take a parent's. The name over their head never changes. Off: no family names are shown; the Book of Families, the Family page and printed trees go by first names.

aliveworkplace.config.heartEvents.toolti: At 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 hearts a villager walks up when they're off work and tells you something about their life; it becomes part of their life story at the Village Hall. Off: nobody starts telling; what was told stays.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.born_here.1: You've been good to me, %2$s, so I'll tell you where I come from. It isn't far. I was born right here in %3$s.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.born_here.2: %4$s is my mother and %5$s is my father. They say I cried loud enough to set the hall bell humming.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.born_here.3: I learned to walk on these paths. I know which roofs leak, and which hens bite.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.born_here.4: People ask if I'll ever leave. Why would I? Everyone I'd miss is within shouting distance.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.traveller.1: Did you know I wasn't born here, %2$s? I walked in off the road with one bag and sore feet.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.traveller.2: I only meant to sleep a night at the inn. The stew was hot, and nobody asked where I'd been.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.traveller.3: Then somebody put down good coin for me to stay. That was %8$s. I've been unpacking ever since.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.traveller.4: I've slept under a lot of roofs. %3$s is the first one I'd call mine.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.traveller.5: So if I fuss over the travelers at the inn, now you know why. I was one of them.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.before_hall.1: You want to know where I come from, %2$s? Here. I was here before here had a name.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.before_hall.2: There was no hall then, no bell, no list with us on it. Just a few doors and a well.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.before_hall.3: Then the hall went up and somebody wrote %3$s over the door. I had to practice saying it.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.before_hall.4: It's a good name. But between us, I still think of this place as just home.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.back_from_gra: I'll tell you something I don't tell many, %2$s. I died once. There's a stone out there that had my name on it.
I remember it going quiet, the way the square does after the last lantern is put out.
It wasn't cold, and it wasn't frightening. It was a long sleep with the door left open a little.
Then someone called me by name. I smelled rain on turned soil, and I was standing in %3$s again.
So I don't hurry much now. Every morning since has been one I wasn't owed.
chronicle.aliveworkplace.heart_event.bef: %1$s told %2$s about %3$s before it had a name
chronicle.aliveworkplace.heart_event.bac: %1$s told %2$s what they remember of the grave
life_story.aliveworkplace.traveller: Came to %3$s as a traveler and was hired at the inn on %8$s
life_story.aliveworkplace.before_hall: Lived here before the hall, when %3$s had no name
life_story.aliveworkplace.back_from_grav: Died, and was brought back from the grave
screen.aliveworkplace.life_story.title: The life story of %s
screen.aliveworkplace.life_story.about: Their family, and what they have told their friends
screen.aliveworkplace.life_story.name_da: A gift on their name day counts three times
screen.aliveworkplace.life_story.to_tell: %s has something to tell you: find them when they're off work
screen.aliveworkplace.life_story.next_he: They'll have something to tell you at %s hearts
They'll have something to tell you at %s heart
screen.aliveworkplace.life_story.empty_h: Make friends with %s: at 2 hearts they'll have something to tell
heart_event.aliveworkplace.station.free: Nobody works at the %1$s near the hall. Could you see me as the village's next %2$s?
heart_event.aliveworkplace.station.none: Every bench in the village already has someone at it. Maybe mine hasn't been built yet.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.station.nitwi: They say no bench would have me, and maybe they're right. I'd still like to be good for something.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_building: You've watched me work, %2$s. Let me tell you about the first wall I ever raised.
I was so proud of it that I leaned on it to admire the view. It leaned too. Then it lay down.
My teacher made me pick up every stone and build it again, with a string and a level this time.
That second wall still stands. I look it over whenever I pass, and I've never leaned on it since.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_mining.1: Do you know what dark is, %2$s? I thought I did, until the day my lamp went out underground.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_mining.2: I'd gone further down than I'd told anyone. One drip from the roof, a hiss, and that was that.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_mining.3: I sat still and counted my breathing. Then I put a hand on the wall and followed it, one step at a time.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_mining.4: It took the whole afternoon to walk back what had taken me an hour to walk in.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_mining.5: Now I carry two lamps and tell someone where I'm going. The dark only had to teach me once.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_land.1: People think my work is all sunshine, %2$s. Let me tell you about the year the harvest failed.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_land.2: The rain came late, and then all at once. What didn't wash away rotted where it stood.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_land.3: We counted what was left and shared it by the handful. Nobody in %3$s got fat that winter, but nobody was left out.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_land.4: In spring one row came up anyway. I've saved seed from it every year since.
I'll tell you why I do this work, %2$s. There was a foal once, born too early, on a cold night.
Its mother wouldn't have it. So I wrapped it in my own blanket and slept in the straw beside it.
I fed it by hand every few hours for a month. I was so tired that I said good morning to fence posts.
It grew taller than me and never once forgot who I was. After that I couldn't have done anything else.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_water.1: Everyone who fishes has one story, %2$s, and this is mine. It's about the fish that got away.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_water.2: It took my line at dawn and pulled me along the bank until noon. My arms shook for two days after.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_water.3: I saw it once, just under the surface. As long as a door, I swear, and looking straight at me.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_water.4: Then the line went slack. I still fish that same bend, and I think it knows I do.
Do you want to know what made me a cook, %2$s? One dish. I didn't even mean to make it.
My grandmother was ill, and all we had in the house was a pumpkin, an egg and the end of the sugar.
I baked what I could out of that. She ate two slices and asked who had taught me. Nobody had.
I've cooked finer things since. That pie is still the only one people ask me for by name.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_learning: I used to be certain about everything, %2$s. Then a book changed my mind.
It was a dull-looking thing with half its cover gone. I only opened it to prove it wrong.
By the last page I'd run out of arguments. I sat there until the candle went out.
I've been less sure and better company ever since. I still keep it where I can see it.
There's something you should know about my work, %2$s. It doesn't always end well.
There was a patient I couldn't save. I did everything I'd been taught, and then things I hadn't.
I sat with them to the end, because that was all there was left to do.
For a while I thought I should stop. Then someone else knocked, and they needed me that same night.
I still think of the one I lost. It's why I'm careful with everyone else.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_arms.1: You think I'm steady, %2$s. I wasn't always. Let me tell you about my first raid.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_arms.2: The bell rang in the night. I had my boots on the wrong feet, and my hands wouldn't stop shaking.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_arms.3: I didn't do anything brave. I stood in the gap where I'd been told to stand, and I didn't move.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_arms.4: By morning they were gone, and everyone in %3$s was still there to be counted.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_arms.5: That's all the work is, really. You stand where you're needed, and you stay.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_trade.1: Since we're friends, %2$s, I'll tell you about the worst bargain of my life. Don't repeat it.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_trade.2: A stranger sold me a compass that pointed, he swore, to whatever I wanted most. I paid a month's earnings for it.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_trade.3: It points north. It has only ever pointed north.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_trade.4: I kept it. When a deal sounds too good, I take it out and look at it. Nobody has cheated me twice.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_music.1: There's a song I know that nobody sings any more, %2$s. I only have half of it.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_music.2: An old woman used to hum it over her washing when I was small. I never asked her for the words.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_music.3: By the time I thought to ask, she was gone, and so was everyone else who knew it.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_music.4: So I play the half I have and make up the rest new each time. I think she'd have laughed at that.
Do you remember your first partner Pokémon, %2$s? I remember mine. I think of it every day.
It was small and stubborn and wanted nothing to do with me. It sat with its back to me for a week.
Then one morning it was asleep on my boots, as if it had always meant to be there.
Everything I know about Pokémon started that morning. The rest has only been practice.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_none.1: Everyone here has their work, %2$s. I watch them go off to it every morning.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_none.2: I haven't found my place yet. I've tried a few things, and they fit me like someone else's boots.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.work_none.4: You've seen more of the world than I have. Tell me what you think, next time. I'd listen to you.
Can I tell you what keeps me up at night, %2$s? It's a small thing. It's the larder.
I lie there counting meals. How many are in the store, how many of us there are, how many days that makes.
The numbers never come out the way I'd like, and an empty stomach gives poor advice in the dark.
I don't say it by day, when everyone has enough to carry. But I can say it to you.
Do you want to know what keeps me up at night, %2$s? Mostly it's having nowhere to lie down.
I don't have a bed of my own. I sleep where there's room, and I'm gone before anyone needs the space.
It isn't the hard floor I mind. It's waking up and not knowing which corner is mine.
One day I'd like a door to close and a pillow nobody else has borrowed. It isn't much to want.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.night_raids.1: I'll tell you what keeps me up at night, %2$s. I listen.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.night_raids.2: Every creak is a boot. Every dog that barks is barking at them. I know it's foolish, and I listen anyway.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.night_raids.3: There's been trouble too close to %3$s lately. You've seen it. We all pretend we haven't.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.night_raids.4: I check the latch twice. Then I lie there working out which way I'd run, and who I'd wake first.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.night_raids.5: It helps that you're about. I sleep better on the nights I know you're near.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.night_illness: Something has been keeping me up at night, %2$s, and I'd rather say it to you than to the ceiling.
There's sickness in my house. You hear a cough differently when it's under your own roof.
I get up to check on things that don't need checking. I boil water nobody asked for.
They tell me it passes, and I believe them by day. It's at night that I need telling again.
Do you know what keeps me up at night, %2$s? The quiet. There's so much of it.
Everyone goes home to someone. I go home, and the only thing that has moved is the dust.
I talk to myself a little, just to hear how the day went. I'm not much of a listener.
So if I keep you talking longer than I should, that's why. Thank you for stopping.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.night_you.1: Do you want to know what keeps me up at night, %2$s? I'm fed, I'm housed and I'm well. So it's you.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.night_you.2: You go off down the road with a sword and a sandwich, and none of us know where.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.night_you.3: I've caught myself listening for your step on the path, like a parent waiting up.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.night_you.4: Come back in one piece, that's all I ask. And knock when you do, whatever the hour.
I want to tell you about the people I love, %2$s. It's a short list, and %6$s is at the top of it.
We were married on %9$s. I remember it better than I remember this morning.
I said my words wrong, and %6$s laughed, and then the whole of %3$s laughed with us.
We've quarreled since, over nothing, the way you only can with someone who's staying.
If you ever wonder why I hurry home in the evening, that's why.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.love_courting: Can you keep a secret, %2$s? It isn't much of one. Half of %3$s has guessed already.
It's %6$s. I find reasons to walk past, and I forget every one of them when I get there.
We haven't said anything grand yet. We talk about the weather as though it were very interesting.
But I think we will, soon. I wanted you to hear it from me before you heard it from the others.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.love_parent.1: You've met my family, haven't you, %2$s? I mean %7$s. That's where my heart lives.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.love_parent.2: Nobody tells you how loud a house gets, or how quickly you stop wanting it quiet.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.love_parent.3: I count heads at supper without meaning to. I expect I always will, long after the last one is grown.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.love_parent.4: If mine turn out kinder than me, I'll have done my work. The rest is only chores.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.love_mourning: I'd like to tell you about %6$s, %2$s. I don't get to say the name out loud very often.
We had our years together, and they were good ones. I wouldn't hand back a single day.
I still set out two cups some mornings. I don't put the second one away as quickly as I should.
People are gentle with me about it. You've been gentle too, without making a show of it.
Loving someone doesn't stop when they do. It has nowhere to go, so I bring it to work with me.
When I think about the people I love, %2$s, I start with %4$s and %5$s. They made me, after all.
My mother taught me to finish what I start. My father taught me when to stop and eat.
There's nobody at my own table yet, and that's all right. I had a good one to grow up at.
I hope I'm half as patient with somebody one day as those two were with me.
Who do I love, %2$s? I've nobody of my own to name. So I'll say it plainly: the village is my family.
The one who saves me the heel of the loaf. The one who complains about my singing. All of %3$s.
Nobody chose me, and I chose all of them. That's worth something too.
And you're on the list now, in case you wondered. You have been for a while.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_content: People ask me what I dream of, %2$s. The truth is, I have everything I wanted.
I'm a Master of my trade. %6$s is waiting for me at home. I wake up glad more days than not.
I used to think wanting nothing would feel like stopping. It feels more like sitting down after a long walk.
So I've no dream to tell you. I have this instead, and I'd like it to be yours.
I've never told anyone what I dream of, %2$s. Don't laugh. I want to be a Master of my trade.
Not for the title. I want to pick up my tools one morning and know there's nothing left to guess at.
I'm not there yet. I can see my own mistakes, and they tell me that's how you know you're on the way.
When it happens, I want you there. Take this now, so you remember who I was before.
I'll tell you what I dream of, %2$s, and you'll think me mad. I want to see the Nether.
Just once. They say the sky is stone there, and that the rivers burn and nobody puts them out.
My whole trade comes up out of the deep. I'd like to stand at the bottom of it and say I've been.
You've been, haven't you? Then take this with you next time, so a part of me has been as well.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_sea.1: Here is what I dream of, %2$s. The sea. I've never laid eyes on it.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_sea.2: I've seen rivers, and I've seen ponds. They tell me the sea is like that, except that it doesn't stop.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_sea.3: I'd like to stand at the edge with my boots off and find out whether it's as loud as they say.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_sea.4: If you get there before I do, take this along. Then one of us will have shown it the sea.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_house.1: Shall I tell you what I dream of, %2$s? It isn't grand. It's a house.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_house.2: A finer one than I have. A proper hearth, a window facing the morning, and a shelf that's only for my things.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_house.3: I've built it so often in my head that I know which stair would creak.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_house.4: Maybe it will stand in %3$s one day. Until then, here. I want you to have something of mine.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_city.1: Do you know what I dream of, %2$s? I dream of %3$s as a City.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_city.2: Lanterns on every corner. A market you can get lost in. Strangers asking me the way, and me knowing it.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_city.3: We aren't that yet. But I remember when we were less than this, and look at us now.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_city.4: You've had a hand in every bit of it. Take this, so that when it's a City you'll remember it small.
heart_event.aliveworkplace.dream_festiva: You'll laugh at what I dream of, %2$s. I dream of a festival, and it's in my honor.
Banners across the square, somebody's terrible speech, and children who have no idea who I am.
I'd pretend to hate every minute of it. I'd keep one of the banners in a drawer for the rest of my life.
It won't happen, and that's fine. Here, take this. You're the one who would have given the speech.
